items.q: Which feature of the data shows that the glider, once released, will move in simple harmonic motion?
options: The force is proportional to the displacement and points the opposite way
The force is zero at the position where the spring is relaxed
The force keeps getting more negative as the glider is moved farther to the right
The force has the same size at equal distances on either side

items.q: What is the spring constant of the spring? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the displacement by the force. The spring constant is force per unit displacement, k = |F|/|x|.
Value: you multiplied force by displacement. k = |F|/|x| = 2.4 N / 0.10 m.

items.q: The glider is pulled to x = +0.080 m and released. What is its acceleration at the moment of release? Take + to the right, include the sign, and give the unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the spring force in newtons. Newton's second law gives a = F/m: divide by the 0.40 kg mass.
Value: the size is right but the direction is wrong. At x = +0.080 m the spring pulls the glider back toward x = 0, so a is negative.

items.q: When the oscillating glider passes x = 0 moving to the right, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero, even though the glider is moving fast
To the right, in the direction it is moving
To the left, because it will soon turn around
Its largest value, because its speed is largest

items.q: Which point is the equilibrium position of the pendulum, and why?
options: Y, where nothing pushes the bob along its path
X, where the bob is momentarily at rest
Z, where the bob stops before turning back
Y, because the bob is moving fastest at that point

items.q: What is the amplitude of the pendulum's motion, measured as an angle?
Why is this pendulum a good example of simple harmonic motion?
options: At small angles the restoring force along the arc is close to proportional to the bob's displacement
The string pulls the bob toward the pivot with a force that stays the same at each point
The bob's weight pulls it down, and gravity is a force that is the same everywhere
The bob moves along a curved path, so it returns to its starting point each cycle

items.q: The same pendulum is released from 60° instead. Which statement is best?
options: The motion is periodic but noticeably less like SHM, because sin 60° is well below 60° in radians
The motion is still SHM, because a pendulum oscillates about Y at any angle
The motion is no longer periodic, because the bob speeds up too much at Y
The motion is closer to SHM, because a larger angle gives a larger restoring force

items.q: An object moves back and forth along the x-axis about x = 0. Which force on it, written as a function of its position x, gives simple harmonic motion?
options: F = −(6.0 N/m²)x²

items.q: A ball bounces straight up and down on a hard floor, rising to the same height each time. Why is this periodic motion but not simple harmonic motion?
options: In the air the force on it is its constant weight, not a force proportional to its distance from a center
The ball is not attached to a spring, so there is no restoring force acting on it at any point of its motion
The ball does not return to the same height, so the motion does not repeat
The ball moves fastest at the top, so its speed pattern is reversed

items.q: A block on a spring slides back and forth on a frictionless table. A meterstick beside it shows that its front edge moves between the 0.12 m mark and the 0.38 m mark. What is the amplitude of the motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the distance from one turning point to the other, which is twice the amplitude. Amplitude is measured from the middle.
Value: that is a meterstick reading, not a displacement from equilibrium. Equilibrium is halfway, at 0.25 m.

items.q: A 0.50 kg block hangs at rest from a vertical spring with spring constant 40 N/m. How far is the spring stretched from its relaxed length at the block's equilibrium position? Use g = 9.8 m/s². Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the mass by k. The spring must balance the weight, mg = 4.9 N, so stretch = mg/k.

items.q: The block hanging from the vertical spring is pulled down and released. When it is at its lowest point, what is the direction of the net force on it?
options: Upward, toward the equilibrium position
Downward, because its weight pulls down
Zero, because it is momentarily at rest
Downward, in the direction it was moving

items.q: A cart on a horizontal spring oscillates between x = −A and x = +A. Where is the size of its acceleration greatest?
options: At x = −A and x = +A
At x = 0
At x = −A/2 and x = +A/2
The same size at each position along the track

items.q: A block on a horizontal spring is pulled 0.10 m from equilibrium and released. In a second trial the same block on the same spring is pulled 0.20 m. Predict how each quantity in the second trial compares with the first.

variables.name: Size of the spring force at the moment of release
Size of the acceleration at the moment of release

items.q: A spring is replaced by one with twice the spring constant. At the same displacement from equilibrium, how does the restoring force on the block compare?
options: It is twice as large
It is half as large
It is four times as large
It is the same

items.q: What is the period of the 0.20 kg block? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the time for 10 oscillations. The period is the time for one: divide by 10.
Value: that is the frequency (oscillations per second), 10/7.05 s. The period is its reciprocal, T = 1/f.

items.q: From 0.20 kg to 0.80 kg the mass is multiplied by 4. How does the period change, and does that agree with T = 2π√(m/k)?
options: It doubles, which agrees: T is proportional to √m
It quadruples, which agrees: T is proportional to m
It doubles, which disagrees: T should quadruple
It halves, which agrees: a heavier block is pulled harder

items.q: Use the 0.80 kg trial to find the spring constant of the spring. Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided by T instead of T². Squaring T = 2π√(m/k) gives T² = 4π²m/k, so k = 4π²m/T².
Value: you used the time for 10 oscillations as the period. Divide by 10 first: T = 1.41 s.

items.q: The student wants a straight-line graph whose slope gives the spring constant. What should be plotted?
options: T² against m; the slope is 4π²/k
T against m; the slope is 2π/k
T against √m; the slope is k/2π
T² against m; the slope is k/4π²

items.q: Which two pendulums have the same period?
options: Pendulums 1 and 2
Pendulums 1 and 3
Pendulums 2 and 4
Pendulums 3 and 4

items.q: What is the period of pendulum 3? Use g = 9.8 m/s². Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you used √(g/ℓ). The length goes on top: T = 2π√(ℓ/g).
Value: you left out the 2π. T = 2π√(ℓ/g).
Value: you used the bob's mass in place of the length. The period of a pendulum does not depend on the mass: T = 2π√(ℓ/g).

items.q: How does the period of pendulum 3 compare with the period of pendulum 1?
options: Twice as long
Four times as long
Half as long
The same

items.q: Pendulum 1 is taken to the Moon, where g is about one sixth of its value on Earth. What happens to its period?
options: It increases, by a factor of about 2.4
It increases, by a factor of about 6
It decreases, by a factor of about 2.4
It stays the same, because ℓ is unchanged

items.q: A child on a swing completes 12 full swings (out and back) in 30.0 s. What is the frequency of the swinging? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the period, the time for one swing. Frequency is cycles per second: f = 12/30.0 s.

items.q: What length of simple pendulum has a period of 2.0 s? Use g = 9.8 m/s². Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you used 1.0 s, the time for one swing across. A period is a full cycle, there and back: T = 2.0 s.
Value: you used T instead of T². Squaring T = 2π√(ℓ/g) gives ℓ = gT²/4π².

items.q: A block oscillates on a horizontal spring. Predict how its period changes for each separate change.

variables.name: The block is replaced by one with twice the mass
The block is pulled twice as far before release
The spring is replaced by a stiffer one

items.q: A simple pendulum swings through a small angle. Predict how its period changes for each separate change.

variables.name: The bob is replaced by one with twice the mass
The string is made four times as long
The pendulum is taken to a planet with a stronger gravitational field

items.q: A student claims that a pendulum with a heavier bob has a longer period, because T = 2π√(m/k) shows that more mass means a longer period. What is wrong with the claim?
options: That equation is for a block on a spring; a pendulum's period is 2π√(ℓ/g), with no mass in it
Nothing: a heavier bob has more inertia, so it does swing more slowly
The equation is right, but a heavier bob also stretches the string, which shortens the period
A heavier bob has a larger weight, so its period is shorter, not longer

items.q: The same block and spring are used horizontally on a frictionless table and then hanging vertically. How do the two periods compare?
options: They are equal
The vertical one is longer, because gravity stretches the spring
The vertical one is shorter, because gravity adds to the restoring force
The horizontal one is longer, because there is no gravity to pull it back

items.q: A 0.250 kg block is attached to a spring with spring constant 40.0 N/m. What is the period of its oscillation? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you used √(k/m). The mass goes on top: T = 2π√(m/k).
Value: you left out the 2π. T = 2π√(m/k).

items.q: You want to double the period of a block oscillating on a spring by changing only the block. What mass should the new block have, if the old one has mass m?
options: 4m
2m

items.q: What is the period of the cart's motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the time from one turning point to the other, half a cycle. A period ends when the cart is back at +0.15 m moving the same way.

items.q: At which time is the cart moving fastest?
What are the directions of the cart's velocity and acceleration at t = 0.50 s?
options: Velocity +, acceleration +
Velocity −, acceleration +
Velocity +, acceleration −
Velocity −, acceleration −

items.q: The cart is stopped and released again from x = +0.075 m. Which graph feature changes, compared with the graph shown?
options: The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is unchanged
The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is halved
The peaks are the same height, and the time between them is halved
The peaks are half as high, and the time between them is doubled

items.q: What is the period of the block's motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied 2π by the frequency. In x = A sin(2πft), the number multiplying 2πt is f = 2.5 Hz, and T = 1/f.
Value: 2.5 is the frequency in hertz. The period is T = 1/f.

items.q: What is the block's position at t = 0.050 s? Include the sign and the unit.

mistakes.why: Value: your calculator was in degree mode, so it took sin(0.785°). The angle 2π(2.5)(0.050) = 0.785 is in radians.

items.q: Where is the block, and how is it moving, at t = 0?
options: At equilibrium, moving in the + direction at top speed
At x = +0.040 m, momentarily at rest
At equilibrium, momentarily at rest
At x = −0.040 m, moving in the + direction

items.q: At t = 0.10 s, which describes the block?
options: At x = +0.040 m, with zero velocity and the largest acceleration, in −x
At x = 0, with the largest velocity and zero acceleration
At x = +0.040 m, with the largest velocity, in +x
At x = −0.040 m, with zero velocity and acceleration in +x

items.q: Two identical blocks on identical springs are released from rest at the same moment, block 1 from 3.0 cm and block 2 from 6.0 cm. Which block returns to its release point first?
options: They return at the same time
Block 1, because it has a shorter distance to travel
Block 2, because it is pulled back by a larger force
Block 1, because its smaller force means less acceleration

items.q: An object in simple harmonic motion is at x = +A/2 and moving toward equilibrium. Which describes its velocity and acceleration?
options: Velocity −, acceleration −, so it is speeding up
Velocity −, acceleration +, so it is slowing down
Velocity +, acceleration −, so it is slowing down
Velocity −, acceleration zero, so its speed is constant

items.q: A cart on a spring moves according to x = (0.12 m) cos(2π · 0.50 t). What is the first time after t = 0 at which the cart is at x = +0.060 m? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is a quarter of the period, when the cart reaches x = 0. Half the amplitude is reached sooner: solve cos(πt) = 0.5.
Value: you used the angle 60 in degrees as if it were radians. cos⁻¹(0.5) = π/3 rad.

items.q: A block on a spring is released from rest at x = +A at t = 0. Which equation describes its position?
options: x = A cos(2πft)
x = A sin(2πft)
x = −A cos(2πft)
x = A sin(2πft) + A

items.q: A block oscillates on a spring with amplitude A. It is stopped and set oscillating again with amplitude 2A. Predict how each quantity compares with the first motion.
The velocity of an object in SHM is graphed against time. At an instant when the velocity graph crosses zero going from positive to negative, where is the object?
options: At its largest positive displacement, x = +A
At its largest negative displacement, x = −A
At equilibrium, moving in the − direction
At equilibrium, moving in the + direction

items.q: A mass on a spring oscillates with amplitude 0.050 m and period 0.50 s. What is its largest speed? (Its speed is greatest at equilibrium and equals 2πA/T.) Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the amplitude by the period with no 2π. In one period the object goes around a full cycle; its top speed is 2πA/T.
Value: 4A/T is the average speed over a cycle. The top speed, at equilibrium, is larger: 2πA/T.

items.q: What is the total mechanical energy of the glider-spring system? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the ½. Spring potential energy is U_s = ½kx².
Value: you did not square the displacement. U_s = ½k(Δx)².

items.q: What is the glider's speed as it passes x = 0? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is v². Take the square root: v = √(2K/m).
Value: you used K = mv² without the ½. ½mv² = 0.36 J gives v = √(2 × 0.36 J / 0.50 kg).

items.q: What is the glider's kinetic energy at x = +0.060 m? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the spring's potential energy at x = 0.060 m. The kinetic energy is the rest of the total: K = E − U_s.
Value: halfway in position is not halfway in energy. U_s = ½kx² goes as x², so at x = A/2 the spring holds a quarter of E.

items.q: Which statement explains why the glider's speed is the same each time it passes x = 0?
options: With no friction, the system's energy stays fixed, and at x = 0 it is all kinetic
The spring force at x = 0 is zero, so the glider's speed at that point stays fixed
The glider's momentum is conserved, because the spring force is internal to the glider
The period does not depend on the amplitude, so each pass at x = 0 takes the same time

items.q: What is the kinetic energy of the block at moment 4? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the spring's potential energy. K is the rest of the 0.36 J total.

items.q: At which moment is the block at its equilibrium position?
options: Moment 3
Moment 1
Moment 2
Moment 4

items.q: At moment 2, what is the block's displacement as a fraction of the amplitude A?
The block is stopped and set oscillating again with twice the amplitude. What is the total energy now?

A block on a horizontal spring oscillates with amplitude A. The same block is set oscillating on a spring with four times the spring constant, with the same amplitude A. Predict how each quantity compares with the first motion.
A pendulum is released from rest at a small angle. Which describes the energy of the pendulum-Earth system as the bob swings from the release point to the bottom?
options: U_g decreases and K increases by the same amount
Kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy both increase
The total energy decreases, because the bob speeds up and uses energy
Gravitational potential energy stays the same, because the bob's mass is unchanged

items.q: In SHM with no friction, which quantity has the same value at every point in the motion?
options: The total mechanical energy
The kinetic energy of the object
The potential energy of the system
The speed of the object

items.q: A 0.20 kg block on a spring with k = 80 N/m passes x = 0 at 0.60 m/s. What is the amplitude of its motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you did not take the square root. ½kA² = ½mv² gives A = v√(m/k).
Value: you put k on top. A = v√(m/k).

items.q: Where in a block's oscillation are its kinetic energy and the spring's potential energy equal?
options: At x = ±A/√2
At x = ±A/2, halfway out
At x = 0, the equilibrium position
At x = ±A, the turning points

items.q: A student says: "At the turning points of a mass on a spring, the energy is zero, because the mass is not moving." What is the error?
options: K is zero there, but the spring holds the energy as U_s
The mass is moving at the turning points, so its kinetic energy is not zero
The energy is zero at equilibrium instead, because the spring is relaxed there
There is no error: the energy drops to zero and is restored by the spring

items.q: A 0.30 kg pendulum bob is released from rest 0.080 m above its lowest point. What is its speed at the lowest point? Use g = 9.8 m/s². Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is v². Take the square root: v = √(2gΔy).
Value: you lost the factor of 2. mgΔy = ½mv² gives v = √(2gΔy).

items.q: The amplitude of a block's oscillation on a spring is tripled. By what factor does its largest kinetic energy change?
